newsitem.title: CYPRUS: DARTS BUFFS PLAY FOR CHARITY IN DIVIDED CYPRUS.
newsitem.headline: DARTS BUFFS PLAY FOR CHARITY IN DIVIDED CYPRUS.

text.p: Hundreds of darts buffs from rival Greek and Turkish communities in Cyprus join forces on Sunday to play for thalassaemia sufferers on both sides of the barbed wire splitting the island.
"It is a sporting event which will be non political in aid of charity," said Greek Cypriot Tom Thoupos, one of the organisers.
"There will be about 200 in attendance from this side and an equal or greater number from the other side," he said on Friday.
The event, in the medieval abbey of Bellapais in the Turkish held north of the island, is sponsored by the United Nations peacekeeping force in Cyprus, UNFICYP.
It will kick off with blood donations by the players.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkish forces invaded the island's north in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia backed by the military junta ruling Greece.
Contact between the two communities now remains limited to a smattering of professional groups meeting under U.N. auspices to discuss issues of mutual interest.

"We try to sponsor anything which gives Turkish and Greek Cypriots an opportunity to get together whether in the (U.N. controlled) buffer zone or on the respective sides," said Peter Schmitz, senior political advisor in the peacekeeping force.
The tournament is the return match of the first joint game held in the Greek Cypriot populated south in April 1994.
Playing darts is a popular pastime in Cyprus where virtually every pub has a darts board.
Around 1000 Greeks and Turks are affected by thalassaemia, a hereditary blood disorder which causes anaemia and can be fatal in children.
